wormald.shelfmark: [Oxford, Bodleian Library,] MS Barlow 37 (ff. 1r–45v/47r for the 'Commonplace-book' material)
wormald.laws: None of Liebermann's texts; but among its last 'Commonplace-book' items are the excommunication and penitential rituals that accompany IV Eg in CCCC 265 section b), followed by Carolingian tithe law probably via Burchard of Worms, which Wormald suggests may have replaced IV Eg (p. 219; Table 4.4, pp. 214–15).
wormald.other_contents: A full set of 'Wulfstan Commonplace-book' (canon collection) texts in the CCCC 265 recension (Excerptiones second recension, Penitential of Ecgberht with Ghaerbald's capitulary inserted, etc.), followed by extracts from Burchard of Worms and Ivo of Chartres (pp. 213, 216; Table 4.4).
wormald.overview: Barlow 37, written in the twelfth century, contains the canon collection associated with Archbishop Wulfstan in the same recension as Corpus 265, with excerpts from Burchard and Ivo after it. It matters for the laws because it has the excommunication and penance rituals that surround IV Edgar in Corpus 265, followed by tithe material, which led Wormald to suggest that IV Edgar may have stood in the early form of the collection and been replaced here by more up-to-date continental texts.
wormald.key_quote: Barlow 37 is a twelfth-century manuscript, where a full set of 'Commonplace-book' ingredients are followed by extracts from Burchard of Worms and Ivo of Chartres. (pp. 213–16)
wormald.doubts: Not in the guide (no Anglo-Saxon law text). Wormald writes only 'Barlow 37'; 'Oxford, Bodleian Library' supplied as the usual home of the Barlow MSS — check. Sauer's siglum 'D' (p. 216 n. 207).
verify_notes: Checked pp. 213, 216–17, 219, 221 and Table 4.4 (image: ‘Barlow 37 (ff. 1r–45v/47r)’); checked, no changes.
